Gap markers, diluted tissue pools and the donor allele deficit

chr10 GENOTYPE runs A-C (huehuetenangensis unions), 1270808 (diploperennis), 1273053 (mexicana); 2026-10-16

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

October 16, 2026

Why

Questions of the user, 2026-10-16, while the diploperennis partner runs D-F ran (docs/runs/genotype_diploperennis_partners_chr10.md):

  • gap markers skip the witness veto, so how can they smooth the genotypes of notebook 06;
  • whether the smoothing erases diluted signal, and what that means for mapping;
  • whether the low donor allele frequency is selection against the donor, as in TeoNAM.

Inputs (not in git): small tables in gap_markers_dilution/, made by agent/nb07/collect.sh (log there) from the runs on hazel and from the measurement jobs 1332113 and 1332684; master copy in /rsstu/users/r/rrellan/BZea/ZEAL/genotype/notebook_inputs/gap_markers_dilution/; copy it next to this notebook to re-render. Lines are named by registry NIL id with the sample in parentheses.

1. Where the gap markers come from

A donor’s RTIGER markers are the union sites gap filling called ALT for it (Milestone 9a): its own tier-A sites and gap sites, discovered in other donors. Each gap marker, looked up in the donor’s own discovery (CRISP, then the witness veto, then the tiers):

run donor markers CRISP called other alleles in discovery, tier B or C not called by CRISP removed by witness veto
B Zh.0020_P3 98,184 12 2,050 89,134 6,988
B Zh.0030_P4 104,016 48 4,212 54,069 45,686
C Zh.0020_P3 85,265 11 2,170 76,123 6,961
C Zh.0030_P4 90,488 42 4,145 43,456 42,844
Medians over the markers; tier from the donor’s BC1 pools counted at the union sites.
run donor markers tier A at the union (%) BC1 reads BC1 ALT reads pools with ALT LLR
B Zh.0020_P3 own 99.3 28 9 3 20.3
B Zh.0020_P3 gap 92.6 24 7 3 18.1
B Zh.0030_P4 own 98.4 45 12 5 26.1
B Zh.0030_P4 gap 85.8 41 10 4 21.7
C Zh.0020_P3 own 99.2 28 9 3 20.3
C Zh.0020_P3 gap 92.5 24 7 3 17.9
C Zh.0030_P4 own 98.3 44 12 5 26.0
C Zh.0030_P4 gap 85.8 41 10 4 21.4

Most gap markers are sites the donor’s own CRISP never called (about 90 % for Zh.0020_P3, half for Zh.0030_P4); about 9 in 10 score tier A when the union is counted on the same BC1 reads (bcftools mpileup, MAPQ 20, base quality 20). So gap filling mostly adds sites the BC1 pools support, not promoted tier-B sites. For Zh.0030_P4, 44 % were removed by its witness veto: BC1 reads ALT, its lines do not.

  • Fewer gap markers have an ALT read in the lines, but read depth there is low; inside donor segments, Zh.0020_P3’s gap markers read ALT about as often as its own (HET 36 vs 41 %, ALT 77 vs 78 %).
  • About 6 % of Zh.0020_P3’s testable gap markers (3x its own markers’ share) and a fifth of Zh.0030_P4’s read no ALT: false alleles for this donor. Zh.0030_P4 carries almost no chr10 introgression (notebook 06), so its test is weak.
  • In REF segments gap markers are cleaner: 0.4-1.4 % ALT against 2.6-2.9 % at own markers.

3. Zh00203113 (PN9_SID806): what smoothing did

Line checks of the sample.
run segments REF % ALT HET % ALT ALT % ALT
alone 25 5.3 24.0 70.3
+ parviglumis 7 7.5 38.0 NA
+ mexicana 8 7.4 38.1 NA
  • Run A breaks 1.6-98 Mb into HET pieces; run B calls it REF. There the sample’s own markers read 14-25 % ALT, far above REF noise and below HET: about 0.18 donor allele frequency (/ 0.82, notebook 05), about 2 of the 6 plants HET.
  • Gap markers read half that or less, so they pulled the stretch to REF and the ALT segment at 143-146 Mb to HET.
  • The diluted signal is not lost: run B’s line checks fail the sample (REF 7.5 % ALT, 7 donor segments).

4. Diluted tissue pools across taxa

taxon lines median REF % ALT p90 lines > 3 % lines > 5 % segments, > 3 % segments, <= 3 %
huehuetenangensis 61 1.3 2.7 4 1 1.5 0
parviglumis 601 1.3 2.7 41 5 3.0 1
diploperennis 253 1.7 3.5 37 5 3.0 1
mexicana 712 1.3 2.9 62 5 4.0 1

7-15 % of the samples read more than 3 % ALT in their REF segments, and those also have more donor segments. Read as pools of 6 plants where only some carry an authentic introgression (user, 2026-10-16), plus some low-depth noise.

Hiding diluted signal in REF segments costs about half a point; the deficit is 3-7 points.

The same direction as TeoNAM, where Chen et al. report “an excess of maize alleles” in all subpopulations; within a call set the taxa compare, across call sets only the direction. SNP50K sits lower partly because it calls donor-homozygous segments HET (notebook 06).

Line coverage is the same for parviglumis and mexicana (0.42x and 0.40x), and neither markers nor BC1 coverage predict a family’s frequency. parviglumis is lower through its whole family distribution, not through families without chr10 introgression.

6. Notes (2026-10-16)

  • Gap markers are mostly CRISP misses, not promoted tier-B sites: per-donor CRISP leaves out sites its own BC1 reads score tier A at the union. One CRISP over all BC1 pools and every donor’s witness pool would be the principled form (user); a separate test (agent/diplo_chr10/joint_crisp_test_plan.md).
  • For mapping, calling diluted stretches REF is preferred (user): it puts the error in the large REF class. SNP50K RTIGER calls the same stretches REF: of the bp our runs call REF in samples with REF % ALT > 3, SNP50K calls 96-99 % REF and 1-4 % HET (clean samples: 99.7-99.9 % REF; table below). Unlike SNP50K, which calls donor-homozygous segments HET, the union runs keep the classes separate (segment ALT % nearer 0 / 50 / 100). For choosing samples at a candidate gene the line checks flag the diluted ones (REF % ALT > 3), per sample, not per position: a windowed flag would be a design change.
SNP50K RTIGER states over the bp our runs call REF (run B, 1270808, 1273053; samples in both).
taxon samples group SNP50K REF (%) SNP50K HET (%) SNP50K ALT (%)
diploperennis 215 REF % ALT <= 3 99.7 0.3 0
diploperennis 37 REF % ALT > 3 97.6 2.4 0
huehuetenangensis 57 REF % ALT <= 3 99.9 0.1 0
huehuetenangensis 4 REF % ALT > 3 98.8 1.2 0
parviglumis 351 REF % ALT <= 3 99.9 0.1 0
parviglumis 30 REF % ALT > 3 99.0 1.0 0
mexicana 518 REF % ALT <= 3 99.9 0.1 0
mexicana 53 REF % ALT > 3 96.4 3.6 0
  • Diluted pools are authentic introgressions carried by some of the 6 sampled plants (user); 6 of the 12 planted plants estimate the bulk’s allele frequency well. If the phenotype came from the same plants, their dose is fractional, and neither REF nor HET states it.
  • The donor allele deficit has the direction of TeoNAM’s; dilution explains half a point of 3-7. On chr10 neither a photoperiod-gene dip nor a consistent lowland (parviglumis) deficit across chromosomes is seen: the parviglumis chr10 shift is about 2.4 standard errors of the family mean and other chromosomes differ by 1-2 points in both directions. The genome-wide run decides.
  • Mexicana above parviglumis on chr10, in both call sets (user, 2026-10-16): zealgt 9.3 vs 7.2 % (gap 2.1 points), SNP50K on the same samples 6.3 vs 5.2 % (gap 1.1), mexicana higher in most 5-Mb windows from 10 to 110 Mb. Genome-wide SNP50K shows no difference (6.8 vs 6.8 %; the sign changes between chromosomes). Not yet known for zealgt genome-wide.
  • Tests, once zealgt genotypes cover the genome (family, i.e. donor, as the unit: a family’s samples share one donor gamete and neighbouring windows share segments):
    1. Divergence: per-family donor allele frequency, parviglumis (40) vs mexicana (42), genome-wide and per chromosome; permutation of taxon labels across families (or a mixed model, sample frequency ~ taxon + (1 | family)). The neutral spread of family means, which carries the founder effect, from the zealtiger pedigree simulation (BC1 pools, BC2, three selfings, real map, each family’s pool and sample numbers). Simulated TIL01 reads through the same pipeline, to rule out a detection bias by taxon (TIL01 mapping bias not measured).
    2. Selection: the overall deficit against the neutral pedigree null after a caller calibration per taxon (simulated reads, known truth); per-window segregation distortion against each taxon’s genome-wide mean, shared by all taxa (selection in the B73 background, e.g. near tga1) or in one taxon only (adaptation; Inv4m as the first check, zealhmm analysis/zeal-inv4m-rtiger-genotype.qmd). The HET excess is no test here: a pool of segregating plants reads HET.
